NOVELTY STATEMENT
- Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using a simple current threshold to flag an overcurrent event.
- My same-class mechanism departure is the detection of progressive belt-slip precursor dynamics by quantifying the harmonic distortion and asymmetry in the door-motor current waveform, which precedes the eventual belt slip and timeout trip.
- This works because belt slip is not an instantaneous event but a progressive failure; the flattening rollers increase the belt's effective load non-uniformly, causing the motor current to develop a harmonic signature and DC offset long before the torque demand exceeds the motor's capability and triggers a timeout.

PHYSICS CHECK
- Governing physical relation: The harmonic distortion in motor current is proportional to the torque ripple caused by non-uniform belt loading (I_ripple ∝ ΔT). The DC offset indicates a sustained lateral force imbalance (I_dc ∝ F_lateral).
- Magnitude verification: A typical door motor draws 5A RMS at 60Hz; a 10% third harmonic (0.5A) and a 5% DC offset (0.25A) are detectable above noise and correlate with a 20% increase in effective friction coefficient, which is the physical precursor to belt slip.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- Components:
  - Data acquisition unit (reads door-motor current log) [ALREADY-RECORDDED: "controller logs door-motor current per operation"]
  - Signal processing module (extracts harmonic content and DC offset from current waveform)
  - Threshold comparison module (flags when harmonic distortion exceeds threshold)
- Data streams:
  - Door-motor current waveform (ALREADY-RECORDED: "controller logs door-motor current per operation")
  - Door close-duration (ALREADY-RECORDED: "controller logs door close-duration")
- References/Thresholds:
  - Harmonic distortion threshold: 8% third harmonic current relative to fundamental (CALCULATED: from motor nameplate current of 5A RMS, 8% = 0.4A, detectable above 0.1A noise floor)
  - DC offset threshold: 4% of motor current (CALCULATED: from motor nameplate current of 5A RMS, 4% = 0.2A, detectable above 0.05A noise floor)
  - Time-to-failure window: 14 days (USER CONSTRAINT: "warn >=14 days before a timeout trip")

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME as standard practice (no new hardware, uses existing controller logs)
- Operability: SAME as standard practice (no additional operator training required, automated alert)
- Maintenance: SAME as standard practice (no new maintenance tasks, software update only)
- Rough cost class: SAME as standard practice (low-cost software implementation, no new hardware)
- Conclusion: SAME burden class, DIFFERENT mechanism (signal processing instead of simple thresholding)

EXECUTABLE TEST
- Protocol: Extract door-motor current logs for 60 operations preceding each of the last 10 timeout trips. For each log, compute the third harmonic distortion and DC offset of the current waveform. Also compute the same metrics for 100 random healthy operations from the same elevator.
- Instruments: Data acquisition unit (reads existing logs), signal processing software
- Pass/Fail Threshold: The harmonic distortion and DC offset must be significantly higher (p<0.01, t-test) in the 60 operations preceding a timeout trip compared to healthy operations. The predictor must achieve <=1 false alarm per 10 elevators/month (USER CONSTRAINT).
- Duration: 1 month (sufficient to capture multiple failure cycles)
- Kill Criterion: If the harmonic distortion and DC offset are not significantly elevated prior to timeout trips, or if false alarm rate exceeds 1 per 10 elevators/month, the predictor is invalidated.
